 MMA UFC 334 Live Updates, Highlights and Results
 Tom Taylor Nov 14, 2026 
 Saturday's UFC 334 carried on the MMA promotion's tradition of entertaining November cards in New York City. 
 This time around, the headlining spot went to a heavyweight title fight, with champ Ciryl Gane taking on unbeaten challenger Josh Hokit. While many fans and pundits expected a finish materialize, the fight turned out to be a thrilling five-round war, with the champ Gane winning a narrow unanimous decision. 
 The co-main event was arguably even more significant, as women's bantamweight champ Kayla Harrison defended her title against returning legend Amanda Nunes. Nunes seemed to have the champ in trouble on the feet early, but gradually succumbed to a grappling assault, and ultimately tapped to a rear-naked choke in round four. 
 Other big winners of the night included Caio Borralho, who outworked Yousri Belgaroui in a middleweight fight, and Luis Gurule, who mounted a huge upset against Bilal Hasan. 
 The card also featured the final fight of welterweight legend Stephen "Wonderboy" Thompson, who retires following a highlight-reel KO of Charles Ratdke. 
 Here's a complete recap of all the action as it happened. 
 Full UFC 334 Card 
 Heavyweight: Ciryl Gane def. Josh Hokit by unanimous decision 
 Women's Bantamweight: Kayla Harrison def. Amanda Nunes by submission (rear-naked choke) at 1:29 of round 4 
 Middleweight: Caio Borralho def. Yousri Belgaroui by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27) 
 Welterweight: Uros Medic vs. Kevin Holland ends in majority draw (28-28, 29-27, 28-28) 
 Flyweight: Luis Gurule def. Bilal Hasan by split decision (28-29, 29-28, 29-28) 
 Welterweight: Stephen Thompson def. Charles Radtke by KO (spinning wheel kick) at 2:54 of round 3 
 Lightweight: Chris Duncan def. Drew Dober by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28) 
 Lightweight: Terrance McKinney def. Jim Miller via KO (punch) at 1:53 of round 1 
 Middleweight: Cesar Almeida vs. Donte Johnson by TKO (punches) at 3:20 of round 1 
 Lightweight: Melquizael Costa def. Jared Gordon by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28) 
 Women's Bantamweight: Bia Mesquita def. Macy Chiasson by submission (rear-naked choke) at 3:23 of round 1 
 Bantamweight: Juan Diaz def. Alateng Heili by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27) 
 Lightweight: Evan Elder def. Samuel Sanches by unanimous decision (30-26, 30-26, 30-26) 
 Live Updates
 47 Total Posts
 Newest First ​ 2 hours ago 10:21 PM 3 Takeaways from UFC 334
 Jeff Bottari/UFC via Getty Images 
 Fight fans have a lot to discuss after Saturday's thrilling UFC 334 card in New York City.
 Here are three big takeaways from the night.
 Ciryl Gane Showed a New Side of Himself 
 Ciryl Gane has always been an impressive heavyweight, but we've never really seen him in any grueling, five-round wars, so it was hard to say what he was really made of. After UFC 334, there is no questioning his heart. Josh Hokit put immense pressure on him from the opening bell in a clear attempt to gas him out and break him down. Not only did Gane's cardio hold up, but he continued to fire back through the entire fight, and showed remarkable durability and tenacity in the process. It was surely not the kind of fight he wants to have every time out, but now we know he can really dig deep when the situation requires him to. Hats off to him.
 Amanda Nunes Failed Herself 
 Amanda Nunes may be the greatest female fighter in MMA history, but in her long-awaited UFC comeback against reigning bantamweight champ Kayla Harrison, she fought like an inexperienced novice. Despite an obvious edge in terms of striking technique and firepower, she chose to repeatedly engage Harrison in grappling exchanges, even when it was very clear those exchanges were not going well for her. Had she focused on boxing, she might well have knocked Harrison out to reclaim the title. She certainly hurt her when she applied pressure on the feet. Instead of doing the obvious thing, however, she favored an utterly foolish game plan that allowed Harrison to dominate her on the mat and submit her in round four.
 'Wonderboy' Got the Retirement He Deserved 
 Retirement fights tend to be pretty ugly in MMA, but Stephen "Wonderboy" Thompson changed the narrative, scoring a highlight-reel, wheel kick KO over Charles Radtke in his final fight. It was one of the best performances of his long career, and the kind of flashiness he was known for in his prime. Fans watching the world over immediately celebrated it, and the fans inside Madison Square Garden made sure he knew how adored he is with a wave of thunderous applause and cheers. It was the kind of storybook ending Wonderboy deserved, not just because he was such a great fighter, but because he's always been such a good role model in a sport where trash talk and bravado are often rewarded.
 2 hours ago 10:16 PM ICYMI: The Judges' Decision After Gane-Hokit
 Gane-Hokit Decision 00:31 
 The French heavyweight remains UFC World Champion.
 2 hours ago 10:15 PM ICYMI: The End of Gane-Hokit
 End of Gane-Hokit Fight 🎇 00:15 
 What. A. Fight.
 2 hours ago 09:59 PM And Still!
 Ciryl Gane is still the UFC heavyweight champion. Josh Hokit had him on the back foot for much of their title fight, but he was firing back and landing for the duration, and had some huge success in the championship rounds, flaunting an impressive gas tank that most people didn't think he had.
 It was an absolutely wild fight—much like Hokit's spring scrap with Curtis Blaydes—and a credit to both men. 
 "This guy is the future, and you saw that tonight," Gane said post-fight, giving his challenger props. "This guy is a motherf*****."
 In victory, Gane is now 15-2, with wins in four of his last five. The lone hiccup in that stretch is his no contest with former champ Tom Aspinall. He's got options from here, notably a trilogy fight with Alexander Volkov, but he will hopefully settle his score with Aspinall at some point.
 This is the first loss of Hokit's MMA career. He's now 10-1 overall, and 4-1 in the UFC. 
 "I will be champion one day," he said before leaving the Octagon. 
 So long as his chin holds up, it's not hard to believe. 
 2 hours ago 09:38 PM To the Championship Rounds!
 Ciryl Gane is still standing after three rounds, but the pace Josh Hokit has put on him is clearly taking a toll. He's a lot less refined than he usually is, seems to have lost a lot of his firepower, and is visibly fatigued. Amazingly, though, he's still landing a ton in return, largely because Hokit doesn't seem to care about defense. 
 Onto the championship rounds. 
 3 hours ago 09:26 PM Off to a Wild Start
 Josh Hokit is putting an unbelievable pace on Ciryl Gane, walking him down with looping shots and takedown attempts. Gane is landing a lot in return, but this is a crazy pace for two heavyweights. Onto round two. 
 3 hours ago 09:08 PM Heavyweight Title on the Line!
 Mike Roach/UFC via Getty Images 
 After 12 fights, it's now time for the main event, and it will be for all the marbles at heavyweight, as champ Ciryl Gane defends against unbeaten, trash-talking challenger Josh Hokit.
 Gane (14-2) claimed the interim heavyweight title with a knockout of Alex Pereira at the White House in June. He was promoted to undisputed champ when Tom Aspinall was forced to abdicate the throne due to lingering eye issues—the result of eye pokes he suffered in a fight with Gane. This will be his first defense of the title. 
 Hokit, who has gained a huge following due to his completely unfiltered persona, is perfect in MMA at 10-0. A former collegiate wrestler and football player, he's gone 4-0 in the UFC, most recently beating Curtis Blaydes by decision in a Fight of the Year contender and then knocking out Derrick Lewis. 
 There will still be questions about the legitimacy of the heavyweight championship no matter who wins this fight, given that Aspinall never lost the belt (like Jon Jones and Francis Ngannou before him). Still, this is a massive matchup between two elite and uncharacteristically nimble big men. 
 Over to you, Bruce Buffer. 
 3 hours ago 09:00 PM And Still!
 Unreal Vid of Kayla’s Sub 🔥 00:21 Kayla Harrison has done it. 
 In the UFC 334 co-main event, the Olympian successfully defended the women's bantamweight title with a fourth-round submission of the returning legend Amanda Nunes. 
 Nunes had some big moments in the fight, visibly hurting Harrison on the feet multiple times—including right before she tapped to a rear-naked choke. However, every time they tied up, Harrison was able to get the fight to the ground, where she was utterly dominant. Nunes managed to avoid a finish through the first three rounds, but it finally came for her in the fourth.
 With the win, which is by far the greatest achievement of her MMA career, Harrison is now a stunning 20-1 as a pro. Her greatness is truly undeniable, and she has arguably surpassed Ronda Rousey as the greatest American fighter in women's MMA history. How much time remains in her career is unclear, but she is a living legend. 
 "I've got a lot of decisions to make when I get home," she said when asked about her fighting future. "Every time I make weight I say never again. We'll see." 
 Nunes, whose game plan in this fight was frankly baffling and totally at odds with her reputation, will now have to stomach the worst loss of her career. Had she taken a different approach, things could have gone much better for her. She's now 23-6 overall. 
 3 hours ago 08:52 PM Strange Game Plan from Nunes
 Amanda Nunes has a clear striking advantage over Kayla Harrison, but for some reason, has chosen to grapple with the two-time Olympic gold medalist in rounds one, two and three, and it has not gone well for her at all.
 We're now headed into the championship rounds, and she has some catching up to do. Nunes needs to get busy with her hands if she wants to win this. 
 4 hours ago 08:20 PM Co-Main Event is Next
 Cooper Neill/UFC via Getty Images 
 We have reached the co-main event of the evening, a women's bantamweight title fight between reigning champ Kayla Harrison and challenger Amanda Nunes.
 It cannot be understated how big this fight is for women's MMA. 
 Harrison (19-1), a two-time Olympic gold medalist in judo, is one of the greatest female athletes in combat sports, period. She's returning from neck surgery, and seems to be very near the end of her career, but has been nothing short of dominant in the cage.
 Nunes (23-5) is simply the greatest female mixed martial artist ever, with wins over legends like Cris Cyborg, Ronda Rousey, Valentina Shevchenko, Miesha Tate, and Holly Holm. A former two-division UFC champ, she never actually lost the bantamweight title Harrison now owns. Instead, she relinquished after a win over Irene Aldana after. After three years away, she returns for one of the toughest fights of her career. 
 It's not often two fighters this decorated get into a cage together. Enjoy it while it lasts. 
 4 hours ago 08:18 PM Borralho Dominates Belgaroui
 Caio Borralho was just too much for Yousri Belgaroui. The Brazilian was in total control of their main card middleweight matchup, scoring multiple takedowns, threatening with submissions, and even stinging the kickboxing transplant on the feet. Belgaroui offered some decent return fire, but there could be no other outcome besides a Borralho unanimous decision win after three rounds.
 "I came to this fight to show that there are levels to this game," the Brazilian said in his post-fight interview. "I have now 33 rounds in this organization. That's a lot of experience.
 "It's belt hunt season," he added. "The Fighting Nerds are taking over."
 With the win, Borralho is now on a two-fight streak, having also recently beaten another Dutchman in Reinier de Ridder. He's an impressive 19-2 overall, and remains one of the top middleweights in the sport.
 This is Belgaroui's first taste of defeat in the UFC after wins in his first three Octagon appearances. He's now 11-3 overall.
 4 hours ago 08:04 PM ICYMI: Kevin Holland Being Kevin Holland
 Funny Kevin Holland Moment 🤣 00:08 
 Never a dull moment with him, eh?
 4 hours ago 07:46 PM Holland vs. Medic Scorecards
 Here are the Kevin Holland vs. Uros Medic scorecards. As you can see, all three judges gave Medic the second round, and one gave him all three rounds before the point deduction—which is pretty much indefensible. 
 That's one of the weirdest scorecards you'll see in MMA. 
 4 hours ago 07:45 PM Middleweight Contenders Collide
 Cooper Neill/UFC via Getty Images 
 The middle bout of the main card will be a big one at middleweight, as Brazilan contender Caio Borralho takes on rising Dutch talent Yousri Belgaroui. 
 Borralho (18-2) was right on the cusp of a title shot until he lost a decision to Nassourdine Imavov late last year. He has since rebounded with a decision defeat of Reinier de Ridder, and will look to make it two in a row against Belgaroui. 
 The Dutch "Boogeyman" is a very experienced kickboxer who battled both Israel Adesanya and Alex Pereira in the ring. Despite some losses in his early MMA career, he's now 11-3 overall, with wins in his last six fights. His most recent three wins were all knockouts in the Octagon, including a stoppage of Djorden Santos last time out.
 This is, without question, the sternest test of the kickboxing veteran's MMA career to date. Borralho is very powerful and extremely versatile. Let's see if he can get a passing grade. 
 4 hours ago 07:42 PM Holland vs. Medic Ends In Draw... Maybe? 
 After controlling his welterweight fight with Uros Medic with his striking and takedowns and benefitting from a point deduction, Kevin Holland seemed to be on track for an upset decision win.
 However, Bruce Buffer then announced the bout as a majority draw. That led to a ton of confusion that left the commentators attempting to decipher the scorecards, and there was some suggestion that Bruce Buffer read the result wrong, but it seems like that's the right reading. 
 With that head-scratcher of a result, Holland stays put at 29-15, and Medic remains at 14-3. The Serbian's impressive four fight win-streak however, is over. It's going to take a real effort to regain the momentum he had before this. 
 We'll let you know if there's any clarification on that bizarre scorecard. 
 5 hours ago 07:23 PM Holland Takes Multiple Low Blows
 Kevin Holland seems to be ahead in his welterweight fight with Uros Medic, but has now absorbed two low blows, and is currently taking his second injury time out. Referee Marc Goddard has taken a point from Medic. 
 Let's see how this affects the outcome. 
 5 hours ago 07:00 PM Will Medic's Rise Continue?
 Jeff Bottari/UFC via Getty Images 
 Uros Medic is one of the hottest contenders in the UFC welterweight division right now. Up next, he'll look to  continue his march toward the title at the expense of fan favorite veteran Kevin Holland.
 At present, Medic (14-3) is riding four straight wins, all by KO. The latest came against Daniel Rodriguez in his home country of Serbia this summer. He also recently stopped Geoff Neal, which is another nice feather in his cap. 
 Holland (29-15), who is a bit of a surprising opponent for Medic at this stage, will look to get his own streak going against the Serbian. In his last fight, he rebounded from a two-fight skid with a decision win over Randy Brown. 
 This one could end any number of ways, on the feet and on the mat. 
 They're on their way to to the cage. Let's get to it. 
 5 hours ago 06:56 PM Gurule vs. Hasan Scorecards
 Luis Gurule vs. Bilal Hasan was definitely a very close fight. Here's how the judges scored it. 
 5 hours ago 06:55 PM Gurule With the Upset!
 Luis Gurule was one of the biggest underdog's on the UFC 334 lineup, but still found a way to beat Bilal Hasan in the main card opener. He pulled off a split decision win with a game plan based on pressure, takedowns, and top control, and actually scored the only knockdown of the fight, dropping his opponent with a right hand in the first round. 
 In victory, he's now 12-4 overall, and 2-4 in the Octagon. This win will completely change the course of his career, and may have even saved his spot on the UFC roster.
 Hasan, meanwhile, tastes defeat for the first time. He's now 10-1 overall, and 1-1 in the Octagon. While he had some success in the fight, out-landing his opponent by almost double on the feet, his grappling his going to be a major concern going forward. He was simply taken down and controlled much too easily. 
 5 hours ago 06:36 PM Early Knockdown for Gurule!
 Despite being a massive underdog against Bilal Hasan, Luis Gurule scored the first knockdown of the fight, dropping his opponent with a big right hand in round one.
 Onto round two!
 5 hours ago 06:32 PM Finally Underway...
 30 minutes after the main card started, the Bilal Hasan vs. Luis Gurule opener is finally underway. 
 Let's see how it goes. 
 6 hours ago 06:10 PM Main Card Starts Now!
 Cooper Neill/UFC via Getty Images 
 It's time for the UFC 334 main card. 
 The fun will kick off in the flyweight division, with red-hot prospect Bilal Hasan taking on Luis Gurule.
 Hasan (10-0) first entered the limelight on Contender Series, knocking out Mridul Saikia to earn a UFC contract. He then repeated the feat in his UFC debut, scoring another sizzling KO over Nilson Rojas. If he keeps winning, he could become a big star in the division, which is arguably better than it's ever been.
 Gurule (11-4) will be looking to play the spoiler, and possibly protect his roster spot in the process. He's gone a tough 1-4 in the Octagon, most recently losing to Rei Tsuruya by submission at bantamweight. 
 This one frankly looks like a freebie for Hasan, but you really never know. Let's see if Gurule can flip the script. 
 6 hours ago 06:06 PM Wonderboy's Final Message
 Wonderboy had a beautiful final post-fight interview with Joe Rogan. You can see a clip of it here. 
 6 hours ago 06:00 PM Wonderboy with the Retirement Stunner! 
 WONDERBOY KO IN FINAL FIGHT 🤯 00:13 Stephen "Wonderboy" Thompson could not have had a better retirement performance. While the 43-year-old faced some adversity in round one of his fight with Charles Ratdke, he began to find his groove in round two, and once he did, he was simply on another level. Despite being at the end of his career, he was in absolutely vintage form, tagging his opponent with crackling kicks and punches to the body and head. Slowly but surely, Ratdke began to wither, and in round three, Wonderboy finally stopped him one for the highlight reel: a dazzling wheel kick to the head. 
 With that, Wonderboy rides off into the sunset with a 18-9-1 MMA record. The karate specialist is undeniably one of the greatest welterweights ever, even though he never won a UFC title. 
 "I've been with the UFC for almost 15 years," he said in his post-fight interview with Joe Rogan. "I couldn't ask better than to to go out with a spinning hook kick to the dome, baby. Let's go!"
 In defeat, Ratdke is back in the loss column after two straight wins. He's now 12-6 overall. 
 6 hours ago 05:40 PM The Final Walk...
 In case you were taking a bathroom break, here's Wonderboy's final walk to the Octagon. 
 6 hours ago 05:35 PM Wonderboy's Last Dance
 Mike Roach/UFC via Getty Images 
 Stephen "Wonderboy" Thompson never got his hands on the UFC welterweight title, despite two attempts. However, he has spent nearly all of his career competing against the best fighters the division has to offer, and has beaten many of them. 
 Up next, at 43 years old, he will compete for a final time opposite Charles Radtke. He will do so with a 17-9-1 overall record, and losses in his last three fights. His most recent defeat was a close split-decision loss to Gabriel Bonfim. 
 Enjoy him while he's here, 'cause he won't be for much longer. 
 Radtke, who will be tasked with spoiling Wonderboy's swan song, is 12-5 overall, and is riding two straight wins. His latest was a decision over Francisco Prado. 
 6 hours ago 05:33 PM Amanda Nunes is In the Building
 After three long years away, the GOAT of women's MMA, Amanda Nunes, has arrived at Madison Square Garden for her title fight with Kayla Harrison. 
 6 hours ago 05:32 PM Duncan Wins Lightweight Firefight
 Chris Duncan and Drew Dober delivered an absolutely awesome fight. Both guys had plenty of big moments over the course of three rounds, but Duncan ultimately landed more, and harder, primarily with his punishing kicks. He also scored a takedown late in round three—at the very moment Dober was starting to come alive. 
 All that worked out to a clear-cut unanimous decision win for the Scotsman. It was one of the best performances of his UFC career to date, particularly in terms of his striking. In victory, he's now 16-3 overall, and back on track after a submission loss to Renato Moicano last time out. 
 Dober is back in the loss column after two-straight KO wins. He's now 19-16 overall. While he'll probably never be a champion, he is one of the most consistently exciting fighters in the game, even in defeat. 
 7 hours ago 05:16 PM Early Land for Duncan!
 Chris Duncan hurt Drew Dober early in round one of their lightweight clash, but Dober managed to survive, and actually landed some nice shots of his own as the round concluded.
 Onto round two!
 7 hours ago 04:59 PM More Lightweight Action on Deck
 Mike Roach/UFC via Getty Images 
 It's time for another fight between two experienced and dangerous lightweights, as Drew Dober welcomes Scotland's Chris Duncan to the USA. 
 Dober (29-15), who holds the record for most knockouts in the lightweight division's history, is riding back-to-back stoppages of Kyle Prepolec and Michael Johnson. However, his current streak was preceded by three straight losses. 
 Duncan (15-3) will be looking to rebounded from a submission loss to Renato Moicano, which ended an impressive four-fight streak. 
 This one should be a lot of fun. 
 7 hours ago 04:56 PM McKinney's Message to the Welterweight Division
 McKinney sent a message to the welterweight division after what he claims was his final lightweight fight. Check it out.
 7 hours ago 04:54 PM Another First-Round Finish for McKinney!
 McKinney 1st-Round TKO 🧨 00:15 It wasn't pretty for Jim Miller fans, but Terrance McKinney picked up yet another first-round win at his expense, ending their catchweight clash with a vicious KO.
 It was a thunderous left hand that finished things.
 With the win, McKinney is 19-9 overall. He has still never reached the scorecards as a pro.
 Now back in the win column, he plans to move up to welterweight, where he'll struggle less with his weight cut. It remains to be seen how that move will go for him, but there are a ton of exciting fights waiting for him at 170 pounds.
 Miller, now 39-20, is back in the loss column after a submission win over Jared Gordon.
 It was tough to see him take this kind of punishment at 43 years old. Hopefully, the UFC will be a little gentler with his matchmaking going forward.
 7 hours ago 04:30 PM A Lightweight Legend Returns
 Cooper Neill/UFC via Getty Images 
 In terms of the potential for excitement, the next fight is one of the best on the whole UFC 334 lineup. 
 This one will pit Octagon legend Jim Miller against Terrance McKinney. 
 The 43-year-old Miller (39-19) is the single most experienced fighter in UFC history, and is trying to hit 30 Octagon wins before retires. He recently recorded his 28th with a submission of Jared Gordon.
 His opponent McKinney (18-9) is the embodiment of live by the sword, die by the sword. Nearly all of his fights end in the first round, whether he wins or loses—and he's done lots of both, going 8-6 in the UFC. In his last fight, he suffered a stoppage loss to King Green in an absolutely wild one-round scrap. 
 It needs to be mentioned, of course, that McKinney missed weight for this would-be lightweight contest by almost five pounds. 
 This one is probably going to end quickly. McKinney fights almost always do. The big question is whether it will bring Miller closer to his goal of 30 UFC wins. 
 8 hours ago 04:24 PM Undefeated No More!
 Jeff Bottari/UFC via Getty Images Donte Johnson is no longer undefeated. 
 The middleweight prospect suffered his first loss inside Madison Square Garden, and it came at the hands of his former training partner, Cesar Almeida.
 Almeida TKOs Johnson 😮 00:20 The Brazilian put an end to things in round one, flooring his opponent with a right hand and finishing him with a series of follow-up punches. Johnson didn't go out right away, but he didn't protest the stoppage at all. He was in big trouble. 
 The win gets Almeida back on track after a knockout loss to Damian Pinas. He's now 8-4 overall.
 Johnson is now 9-1. 
 8 hours ago 04:14 PM 🎥 ICYMI ... the Judges' Decision After Gordon-Costa
 Costa Beats Gordon 00:17 
 The fans at MSG didn't agree with this one.
 8 hours ago 04:10 PM Former Training Partners Collide
 Jeff Bottari/UFC via Getty Images 
 It's time now time for a clash of former training partners at a catchweight of 190 pounds, as Donte Johnson takes on Cesar Almeida. 
 Johnson (9-0) has looked great since joining the UFC, winning his first three fights. Most recently, he scored a nasty first-round KO over Eric McConico. 
 Brazil's Almeida (7-3) has spent nearly all of his pro career in the Octagon, but has been very inconsistent, going 3-3 in six UFC fights. In his most recent appearances, he got to experience Damian Pinas' staggering knockout power. That was his second loss in a row. 
 Let's see if he can turn things around here, and take Johnson's 0 in the process. 
 8 hours ago 04:07 PM Costa vs. Gordon Scorecards
 Check out the scorecards for that very close Melquizael Costa vs. Jared Gordon fight. 
 8 hours ago 04:04 PM Costa Scrapes By Gordon 
 Melquizael Costa had a tough second round against Jared Gordon, as he was forced to fight off takedowns and spent several minutes in bad positions on the mat. That said, he had a fantastic first round, marked by a vicious striking attack, and seemingly won the third based on damage. 
 That's certainly how the judges scored it, as he walked away with a unanimous decision win.
 In victory, the Brazilian striker is now 27-8 overall. This successful lightweight debut separates him from a decision loss to Arnold Allen in his final featherweight fight. 
 Gordon (21-10) has now lost three straight. That said, he certainly had his moments in this fight, and will probably get another shot in the UFC. 
 8 hours ago 03:49 PM Quite an Introduction!
 Melquizael Costa clearly loved the introduction he got from Bruce Buffer. Check it out! 
 8 hours ago 03:30 PM Lightweight Banger Up Next
 Mike Roach/UFC via Getty Images 
 Next up, we've got a fan-friendly lightweight fight between Melquizael Costa and Jared Gordon.
 Brazil's Costa (26-8) was recently on a six-fight win streak down at featherweight, which included a stunning knockout defeat of Dan Ige. However, he recently had his progress slowed by a decision loss to British veteran Arnold Allen, and will seek greener pastures at lightweight. 
 New York's own Gordon (21-9) has never quite broken through as a serious lightweight contender, but has been on the UFC roster for years, and battled some high quality opposition, famously losing a hotly debated decision to a rising Paddy Pimblett a few years back. He's lost his last two fights, first suffering a TKO defeat against Rafa Garcia, then tapping out to a Jim Miller guillotine choke. 
 Costa seems poised to win this one—possibly inside the distance—but Gordon will have plenty of tricks up his sleeve. 
 Let's get to it. 
 9 hours ago 03:26 PM Another Submission for Mesquita!
 Mesquita Locks in Choke 00:24 Make that four submissions in a row for Bia Mesquita!
 The Brazilian grappling specialist made quick work of Macy Chiasson in their undercard bantamweight scrap, coaxing out the tap with a rear-naked choke before the first round was over. 
 Now 9-0 overall and 4-0 in the Octagon, it's fair to call Mesquita one of the most intriguing young contenders in the bantamweight division, which has been starving for new talent for years. Her elite BJJ and her ability to train closely with the division's champ Kayla Harrison have clearly made her a force to be reckoned with. 
 "I trained so hard for this fight," she told Joe Rogan post-fight, before laying out plans for a future title fight, presumably once Harrison has retired. 
 In defeat, Chiasson is now 10-7 overall, with losses in her last four fights. She may have made her last walk to the Octagon. 
 9 hours ago 03:12 PM Can Mesquita Stay Unbeaten? 
 Cooper Neill/UFC via Getty Images 
 The action will trundle on in the women's bantamweight division, where Macy Chiasson will take on Bia Mesquita. 
 Chiasson (10-6) was once a fairly highly regarded contender at bantamweight, but has lost her last three fights, and seems to have fallen a bit behind most of her rivals in the division. 
 Mesquita, a decorated BJJ specialist who trains with Kayla Harrison, is off to an 8-0 start in her MMA career, and has won her first three UFC appearances by submission. Most recently, she tapped Melissa Mullins with a first-round armbar. 
 This is Chiasson's chance to prove she still belongs on the UFC roster, and Mesquita's opportunity to assert herself as a real contender at 135 pounds. 
 Let's get to it. 
 9 hours ago 03:10 PM Diaz By Decision
 Juan Diaz was just a little too quick and a little two slick for Alateng Heili in their undercard fight. While he had to settle for a unanimous decision win rather than a finish, he landed over 50 percent of the strikes he threw at his extremely durable opponent. 
 With this impressive win, the Peruvian is now 17-1-1 overall, and 1-0 in the UFC. His post-fight call for a fight with a ranked opponent is definitely premature, but he clearly has a bright future—assuming he doesn't keep missing weight, like he did for this fight.
 Alateng, who took this fight on very short notice, is now 18-11-2, and 1-1 in his last two. 
 9 hours ago 02:39 PM Bantamweights Up Next
 Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images 
 The second bout of the night will be contested at bantamweight, with China's Alateng Heili taking on Juan Diaz of Peru. 
 Alateng (18-10-2), who took this fight on short-notice, last fought in September, when he defeated John Castaneda by split decision in his 10th UFC appearance. 
 Diaz (16-1-1) earned a UFC contract last year, when he knocked out former ONE Championship title challenger Kwon Won Il. He made his Octagon debut in May, when he submitted Malcolm Wellmaker in round two. Needless to say, he's shown a lot of potential, and is a heavy favorite to win this fight. He did, however, miss weight for this fight. 
 Let's see if "The Mongolian Knight" can flip the script. 
 9 hours ago 02:35 PM Elder Dominates Sanches
 Evan Elder was just a few steps ahead of Samuel Sanches in the UFC 334 main-card opener, rocking his foe on the feet multiple times, and taking him down repeatedly over three rounds. 
 Considering Sanches also lost a point for repeated fence grabs, there could be no other outcome than a unanimous decision win for Elder. 
 That puts Elder on a four-fight win streak. Not bad for a guy who lost his first two UFC fights. He's now 11-2 overall.
